rubric.why: Hypertext is text that contains links.
rubric.description: Defines hypertext as text containing links.
rubric.how: Look for both text and links in the definition.

rubric.why: Links let users move between connected information.
rubric.description: Explains that links provide access between connected information.
rubric.how: Look for the idea that users can move between linked information.

modelAnswer: Hypertext is text that contains links to other text, documents, or related information.
These links allow users to move between connected information.

items.followUp: Compare RAM and ROM with respect to data retention.

rubric.why: Volatile memory loses its data when the power is switched off.
rubric.description: States what happens to volatile memory when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Look for volatile memory, data loss, and power being switched off.

rubric.why: Non-volatile memory retains its data when the power is switched off.
rubric.description: States what happens to non-volatile memory when power is switched off.
rubric.how: Look for non-volatile memory retaining data when power is switched off.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory loses its stored data when the power is switched off.
Non-volatile memory retains its stored data even when the power is switched off.

items.followUp: Name one guided and one unguided transmission medium.

rubric.why: A transmission medium is a path or channel through which data is sent.
rubric.description: Defines the medium as a path or channel for data transmission.
rubric.how: Look for a path or channel through which data is sent.

rubric.why: The medium carries data between communicating devices.
rubric.description: States that the medium carries data between devices or from sender to receiver.
rubric.how: Look for data being carried between devices, or from a sender to a receiver.

modelAnswer: A transmission medium is a path or channel through which data is transmitted from a sender to a receiver.
It carries data between communicating devices.
